text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme Major. The clinical presentation of targetoid lesions on acral surfaces (hands/feet) progressing to mucosal involvement, combined with a lack of significant systemic toxicity and normal initial labs, is most consistent with this hypersensitivity reaction, often triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae (which may not yet be detectable) or herpes simplex virus.
